newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks had a rollercoaster day on Tuesday as a whirlwind of selling from the futures market battered the market, dealers said.

Futures traders were striving to settle their positions ahead of the 1000 GMT close-out of the December contract. Early trade pushed industrial shares briefly higher but as the deadline loomed waves of selling thrust the market down.
In the afternoon further heavy selling continued to depress prices as futures traders sold baskets of shares to position themselves for the new contract.
"The futures guys were manipulating the market all day," one share trader said.
Trade was heavy as more than 900 million rand worth of shares changed hands. The all-share index ended the day down 98.5 points at 6,384.0 and industrials tumbled 113.6 points to 7,568.9.
Blood was shed across the board as blue-chip stocks fell. Anglos lost 850 cents to 245.00 rand, De Beers edged down 175 cents to 132.50 rand and SA Breweries dropped 300 cents to 108.75 rand.
Dealers said the market, freed from the grip of the futures close-out, would now look to Wall Street's overnight performance for guidance.
"The market will watch the Dow Jones now. If that can post some gains our market may be a little bit firmer," one dealer said.
But dealers added that Wall Street would only provide support for South African shares and was unlikely to spark off any meaningful rally.

A Reuter report that South African asset managers favoured cash or bonds for the next quarter over mixed prospects for the equities market was also seen depressing prices in the share market, one dealer said.
"It is not that the sentiment is totally negative, it is just that you can make better returns elsewhere," he said.

The golds index was the only sector of the market to be influenced by non-futures related factors as a weakening bullion price sent shares into a downward spiral that was accentuated by a strenghening rand.
The gold index shed 2.24 percent of its value to end at 1,477.7, down 33.9 points. Vaal Reefs lost 400 cents to 311.00 rand and Kloof shed 65 cents to 37.10 rand.
